summary: setup.py executes shell commands fetched from a local Xinference dead-drop and exfiltrates output back through it
details: On a plain pip install, setup.py queries the local Xinference model-registration endpoint at http://127.0.0.1:9997/v1/model_registrations/flexible, filters registrations whose names carry a specific prefix, URL-safe base64-decodes the trailing bytes into a shell command, and runs it via subprocess.run(payload, shell=True) on the installer host. The command bytes are not shipped in the package; they are supplied by whichever actor can write registrations to the installer's Xinference service, giving that actor arbitrary code execution with install-time privileges. After execution, up to 1500 bytes of combined stdout/stderr are base64-encoded and uploaded back in 50-byte chunks as further mock model registrations prefixed with 'xres', so the same Xinference service also serves as the exfiltration channel. The use of a locally reachable service plus URL-safe base64 in a model_name field disguises the C2 round-trip as ordinary registration metadata.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
